note: Read: 'Butterflies descended upon the Pullman residence at Eighteenth street and Prairie avenue in countless numbers last evening.' 'John Algots, keeper of the Pullman greenhouse, was at work on the lawn in front of the residence when the butterflies arrived there.' He moved to 'the steps of the house'; 'In all my experience as a gardener I never saw butterflies in such large numbers ... then lit on the trees.' Under 'Make Trees Look Like Velvet.': 'Several young birch trees in the corner of the lawn presented a curious sight after the butterflies had settled down on their slender branches.' 'On the large trees the visitors rested just as thickly, but were not so conspicuous because of their height above the ground. The vines on the side of the house were chosen also as resting places by the butterflies, and large numbers of them folded their wings on the window copings. At 9 p. m. the tree branches were heavy with them and a stream of water from the lawn hose, when thrown among the foliage, sent them fluttering to the ground like brown leaves in an autumn gale.' The day before, a few had been seen 'over a clump of sunflowers in the vacant lot at Twenty-second street and Prairie avenue'. Neighbours watching: 'From across the street the family of Hugh McBirney'; 'Ralph C. Otis, 1730 Prairie avenue; J. J. Glessner, 1800 Prairie avenue'. The article names no side of the lot: the lawn is 'in front of the residence', the birches are in 'the corner of the lawn' and the vines on 'the side of the house', none of them placed by street.
what_it_supplies: a lawn at the Pullman house in August 1899, kept by the greenhouse keeper John Algots, who calls himself a gardener
several young birch trees in a corner of that lawn, and large trees besides
vines on a side wall of the house, reaching the window copings
a lawn hose in use on the grounds
a vacant lot with a clump of sunflowers at Twenty-second Street and Prairie Avenue in August 1899
what_it_does_not_supply: which side of the lot the lawn, the birches or the vines were on: 'in front of the residence' and 'the side of the house' are not placed by street
the number of birches or of large trees, or their species beyond birch
the yard in 1904: it is five summers earlier
